title: Court registrars’ strike and sit-ins at multiple courts; episode boundaries unresolved
location: Sidi M’hamed and Dar El Beida courts in Algiers; courts or judicial councils in Constantine, Bouira, and Tizi Ouzou.
scope: Multiple reported court sites; a coordinated national episode versus separate local actions is unresolved.
organizer: Court registrars and clerks; the opened reports do not establish a specific organizer.
participants_original: No headcount. Ennahar qualitatively describes the Tizi Ouzou action as large/crowded.
threshold_50_evidence: No numerical attendance at any site. The qualitative “large/crowded” wording for Tizi Ouzou does not establish at least 50.

occurrence.summary: Opened Ennahar reports describe public sit-ins at courts and a Sidi M’hamed Court sit-in during a registrars’ work stoppage in early January.

start_date.summary: The 3 January Sidi M’hamed article says the strike was on its third day, which suggests 1 January if literal. The 2 January report also uses relative Sunday/Thursday wording with an uncertain date anchor. A separate 30 December sit-in at Sidi M’hamed lasted one day; the sources do not prove it continued into January. Physical onset therefore remains unknown.

end_date.summary: The reports describe ongoing strike/sit-in activity but do not establish physical termination.

location.summary: The opened reports name Sidi M’hamed and Dar El Beida in Algiers, and court or judicial-council sites in Constantine, Bouira, and Tizi Ouzou.

organizer.summary: The reports identify registrars/clerks and discuss union recognition but do not identify an organizer for the reported gatherings.

demands.summary: Requests include the collection-fines benefit, higher wages, better social/work conditions, a separate justice-sector staff status, union recognition, southern allowance, and housing. Tentative broad labor_wage_dispute mapping.

participants.summary: No site has a numeric attendance estimate. Tizi Ouzou is described qualitatively as large/crowded; threshold remains unresolved.

state_target.summary: Demands address the Ministry of Justice and judicial administration; Sidi M’hamed participants met judicial-council officials.

state_response.summary: At Sidi M’hamed the judicial-council president and prosecutor spoke with registrars; requests were said to be under consideration without a deadline. No concrete accommodation is established, and other response dimensions are unreported.

protester_violence.summary: The opened reports do not describe protester violence; absence of reporting is coded unknown.

continuity.summary: The 30 December one-day sit-in and early-January reporting share site/occupation/demands, but no opened source proves uninterrupted physical continuation or resolves whether several local gatherings are one episode.

eligibility.summary: A public gathering is reported, but onset/month ownership, cross-site episode boundaries, and the >=50 threshold remain unresolved; retain as a candidate for review.

notes: January public actions are reported, but source dates/relative wording and the preceding 30 December sit-in do not establish the physical onset or continuity. Two Ennahar pieces are same-outlet follow-ups, not independent attendance confirmation. No threshold is established.
open_questions: What was the physical start date at each site, especially Constantine and Sidi M’hamed?
Were the sites part of one coordinated national event or distinct local actions?
Did any site gather at least 50 people?
When did the strike/sit-ins end, and what event-specific state response occurred?

title: Interprovincial taxi drivers’ sit-in over route licensing and state enforcement
location: Outside the Algiers Transport Directorate in El Biar, Algiers; drivers on Algiers–Mila and Algiers–Ferjioua routes.
scope: Single-site sit-in; broader geographic organization beyond the named taxi routes is not established.
organizer: Drivers on the named interprovincial routes; the report refers to a union representative but does not establish who convened the sit-in.
threshold_50_evidence: The source confirms a sit-in but gives no attendance estimate; the >=50 threshold is unresolved.

occurrence.summary: Opened Echorouk report says taxi drivers held a sit-in outside the Algiers Transport Directorate on 23 January.

start_date.summary: The report dates the sit-in to 23 January 2022.

end_date.summary: Neither report establishes how long the 23 January sit-in lasted. The 2 February gathering is a later same-issue sit-in, not evidence of uninterrupted presence.

location.summary: Outside the Algiers Transport Directorate in El Biar; drivers worked the Algiers–Mila and Algiers–Ferjioua lines.

participants.summary: No attendance count is reported for the January sit-in.

demands.summary: Drivers sought state intervention over an allegedly unauthorized Algiers–Chelghoum Laïd service, an investigation, and instructions to stop that route. The existing category list does not clearly represent this licensing dispute; no forced category assigned.

state_target.summary: The sit-in was outside a state transport directorate and drivers sought intervention by transport authorities/minister.

state_response.summary: The acting director requested a clarifying letter; the union said its file was already on record. No concrete policy accommodation is reported. The source separately mentions driver altercations without linking them to the sit-in.

protester_violence.summary: The separate altercations are not tied to the sit-in or attributed to protesters; event violence remains unknown.

eligibility.summary: A public, state-directed sit-in is documented; attendance threshold remains unknown.

notes: A Jan 19–20 work stoppage is reported separately and held out absent public-gathering evidence. Echorouk’s 2 February follow-up covers the same route dispute but does not establish continuity or January turnout. No attendance number or clear demand-category mapping is available.
open_questions: Did 50 or more people attend the 23 January sit-in?
What administrative action followed the letter request?
Should the licensing demand map to an existing category?
